rubric.why: Identifies autotrophs by their ability to make food themselves.
rubric.description: Autotrophs make or synthesize their own food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that autotrophs make their own food.

rubric.why: Distinguishes heterotrophs by their dependence on other organisms for food.
rubric.description: Heterotrophs cannot make their own food and obtain it from other organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that heterotrophs cannot make their own food or obtain food from other organisms.

modelAnswer: Autotrophs make their own food from simple inorganic substances, using light or chemical energy.
Heterotrophs cannot make their own food and obtain it from other organisms.

items.followUp: What is the role of enzymes in lowering the energy needed for a reaction?

rubric.why: Identifies activation energy as the minimum energy required.
rubric.description: Activation energy is the minimum amount of energy required.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the minimum energy.

rubric.why: Links the required energy to starting a reaction.
rubric.description: This energy is required to start a chemical reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the energy is needed to start a chemical reaction.

modelAnswer: Activation energy is the minimum amount of energy required to start a chemical reaction.

items.followUp: What is a coenzyme? Give one example.

rubric.why: Defines a prosthetic group as a non-protein component firmly attached to an enzyme.
rubric.description: A prosthetic group is a non-protein component tightly or permanently bound to an enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is a non-protein component tightly or permanently bound to an enzyme.

rubric.why: Gives a valid example of a prosthetic group.
rubric.description: Haem in catalase is an example of a prosthetic group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving haem in catalase as an example.

modelAnswer: A prosthetic group is a non-protein component that is tightly or permanently bound to an enzyme.
Haem in catalase is an example.

items.followUp: Explain how food is moved through the oesophagus.

rubric.why: Describes the wave-like muscular action involved in peristalsis.
rubric.description: Peristalsis involves rhythmic contraction and relaxation of muscles in the alimentary canal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the rhythmic or wave-like contraction and relaxation of the muscles.

rubric.why: States the effect of peristalsis on food.
rubric.description: These movements push food forward along the canal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that peristalsis pushes or moves food forward.

modelAnswer: Peristalsis is the rhythmic contraction and relaxation of muscles in the alimentary canal.
These wave-like movements push food forward along the canal.
